newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan hopes driver's death won't hurt Iraq ties.
newsitem.headline: Jordan hopes driver's death won't hurt Iraq ties.

text.p: Jordan said on Monday it hoped the killing last week of one of its embassy drivers on the desert highway to Baghdad would not damage ties with Iraq.

A Foreign Ministry spokesman was quoted by Petra state news agency as saying Jordan was keen not to allow the incident to harm ties as it awaited results of an Iraqi investigation over the shooting of driver Omar Ahmed al-Subh.

Subh's body was found on November 11 about halfway along the 500 km (310 mile) highway between its border and Baghdad. His attackers also stole the embassy's diplomatic bag which contained 250 Jordanian passports and other documents.

"What happened falls under the responsibility of the concerned Iraqi authorities and furthermore it harms ties and the reputation of the Iraqi security...which is a matter which the foreign ministry is keen to avoid happening," the spokesman was quoted by the official state news agency as saying.
Jordan earlier held Iraq's government responsible for the incident, saying it was a violation of international accords guaranteeing the safety of diplomatic couriers.
"The foreign ministry wants to clarify that the government is still awaiting the efforts of the Iraqi governments and its search for the perpetrators of the ugly crime," the spokesman added.

The unnamed official expressed concern over "distorted" press reports that have appeared in the last few days", without elaborating. Many papers have warned the incident could deal another blow to already cool ties with Baghdad.

Jordan was once a close ally of Iraq during a U.S.-led military coalition waged war to expel Baghdad's forces from Kuwait in 1991. But last year King Hussein turned against President Saddam Hussein and called for change in Iraq.
